title: AI Debt Binge Risks Crowding Out EM Nations From Global Markets
source_used: Bloomberg, opening two paragraphs only (paywall); a Briefs Finance rewrite was blocked
key_facts: Bloomberg: the debt binge to finance AI infrastructure is pitting governments against technology giants in a competition for capital.

That is driving up borrowing costs for developing nations, whose yields were already under pressure from geopolitical concerns, elevated oil prices and higher policy rates, according to Bank of America strategists.
quote_evidence: The debt binge to finance artificial intelligence infrastructure is pitting governments against technology giants in a competition for capital.

That's driving up borrowing costs for developing nations, with yields already under pressure due to geopolitical concerns, elevated oil prices and higher policy rates, according to Bank of America Corp. strategists.
why_it_matters_hint: AI borrowing is said to raise financing costs for developing countries.
notes: Bloomberg prefetch holds only two paragraphs (paywall). A Briefs Finance rewrite ('Hyperscalers' Borrowing Is Pushing Up Costs For Emerging-Market Debt') returned a JavaScript wall. Only the lead is used; no figures or country names are claimed.
